subject: Dedicated capacity fit: clarifying TPS, token mix, and GPU tradeoffs
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Dedicated capacity fit: clarifying TPS, token mix, and GPU tradeoffs

Hi Elena — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and the specific clarifying items we need to size a Dedicated pool that matches Brightwell's production needs.

Summary of what we heard on the call:
- Primary workload: customer-facing search + short chat completions.
- Initial traffic profile you mentioned: ~180 requests/sec sustained with daily diurnal patterns and the ability to burst. You flagged occasional marketing-driven spikes up to ~700 rps.
- Average prompt + generation ~350 tokens (you said ~250 prompt, ~100 gen on average).
- Latency SLO target: p95 < 300ms for short searches, relaxed for longer chat flows.
- Preference today: evaluate Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool). Private/VPC could be next phase for compliance.

What we need from you to finalize a sizing recommendation and POC plan:
1) Confirm sustained RPS and the max burst RPS (numbers above are our notes).
2) Token mix breakdown: percent of requests that are short (<64 tokens), mid (64–512), and long (>512).
3) Any hard regional constraints (US regions ok?), and whether persistent KV caching of prefixes is allowed.
4) Security artifacts: SOC2 / encryption requirements — you mentioned sending a short SOC2 summary and a POC requirements spreadsheet.

Next steps from our side once you confirm: Karthik will propose a GPU mix (H100 vs A100 vs L40-style tiers) with concurrency/batching guidance and an estimated token/s throughput target. We’ll also propose a 2-week micro-benchmark kick-off to validate latency and cost assumptions.

Thanks — happy to jump back on a 20–30m call if that helps.

—Connor

Confirmed traffic profile:
- Sustained baseline: 180 requests/sec (production daytime).
- Burst: up to ~700 requests/sec for short 10–20 minute windows (marketing/feature launches).
- Average token profile per request: ~350 tokens total (we measure ~250 tokens in prompt + ~100 tokens generated).
- Token mix: ~68% short (<=64 tokens), ~25% mid (65–512), ~7% long (>512).

Requirements / constraints:
- Data residency: must operate in US (we prefer us-west region).
- Initially we want Dedicated reserved capacity for stability. Private/VPC is on the roadmap but not required for the POC.
- We will share a redacted sample prompt set for the micro-benchmarks.

We attached Brightwell_POC_requirements.xlsx and Brightwell_SOC2_summary.pdf. Please let me know if you need anything else before Karthik proposes the GPU sizing.

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity fit: clarifying TPS, token mix, and GPU tradeoffs

Hi Elena — thanks for the fast follow-up and the token mix. Based on the confirmed numbers (180 baseline, 700 burst, avg 350 tokens) here are pragmatic sizing and tradeoffs for Dedicated: 

Rough throughput math (for planning):
- Sustained tokens/sec = 180 rps * 350 tokens = ~63,000 tokens/s.
- Burst tokens/sec = 700 rps * 350 tokens = ~245,000 tokens/s (short windows).

GPU tradeoffs and recommendation summary:
- H100 (best latency & throughput): highest up-front unit cost but significantly better at high-token workloads and short-latency p95. Good for chat/search SLOs.
- A100 80GB (balanced): slightly cheaper, still strong throughput. Good if you want lower committed cost but still need good batching.
- L40-class (cost-effective for embeddings/batch-heavy generation) — not ideal for p95-sensitive search.

Suggested Dedicated pool for the POC (sensible starting point):
- Start with 4 x H100 nodes in the reserved pool to cover low-latency search/chat traffic. Configure continuous batching with KV-prefix caching for common prompts.
- Add 2 x A100 nodes for background generation/batch work and to absorb burst traffic with graceful routing.

Concurrency & batching notes:
- With an H100-heavy pool and continuous batching, we would expect to serve the sustained 180 rps with headroom and keep p95 < 300ms for short queries. Exact numbers depend on prompt length distribution (which you will share).
- For the 700 rps burst, we recommend autoscale + a short-term burst policy (fallback to A100 nodes) and an optional region-level fallback to ensure availability.

Benchmarks and next steps:
1) We propose a 2-week micro-benchmark: you share ~1,000 representative prompts (redacted), we run latency/cost/batch-efficiency tests on the proposed pool, and return a performance matrix.
2) If the micro-benchmark validates the plan, Redwood will produce an SOW covering committed nodes, pricing, and a POC runbook.

Could you confirm whether you want us to size for the burst peak (700 rps) as hard-reserved capacity or prefer a reserved baseline + burst credits/autoscale? That choice materially affects the committed GPU count.

Happy to jump on a 30m technical sync Dec 29 to kick off the micro-benchmark.

—Karthik
